title: Make your first edit
goal: Change a title, compare it with the original, then practise switching modes.

steps.do: Select Edit. Double-click the large Sales Performance heading. Type Sales performance | Review copy and click outside it.
steps.see: The heading changes and the document chip shows unsaved edits.

steps.do: Choose Home › Undo and look at the heading. Choose Redo to bring your edit back.
steps.see: Undo restores the original title. Redo restores your new title.

steps.do: Choose Interact, then hover a bar on Sales by region.
steps.see: A pop-up appears without selecting the chart. Switch back to Edit before continuing.

title: Build a reader guide
goal: Give someone who has never seen the dashboard a clear place to start.

steps.do: Choose Layout › Tab ribbon on the one-page sample. Then choose Insert › Text tab and name it How to use.
steps.see: The outline shows the dashboard and How to use tabs.

steps.do: Add a short instruction on the new tab. Explain where to start, how to hover a chart and how to return to the overview.
steps.see: You can open the new tab in Interact and follow its instructions.

steps.do: Add a Methodology tab. Say that these are sample sales figures, note the time period, and define net sales.
steps.see: A reader can tell where the figures come from, what they mean and when they apply.

title: Explain one chart
goal: Make one chart answer a question without your narration.

steps.do: In Edit, double-click Sales by region. In Commentary & size add the period and a one-line takeaway. Apply.
steps.see: The chart has a title, units or period, and a takeaway you can verify.

steps.do: In the Tooltip settings choose Label: value for a plain-number display. Apply and hover in Interact.
steps.see: The tooltip names the region and shows a sensible amount. Compare one bar with the original.

steps.do: Check the legend, colours and chart size. Try Fit, then draw at a phone width from View.
steps.see: You can still read the title and know what the chart measures. Note anything that needs a wider layout.

title: Link data, filter and drill down
goal: Learn the difference between a displayed total and the rows behind it.

steps.do: Open Sales by region › Data & drill-down. Use the suggested data, choose region then state, and apply a Sum of sales.
steps.see: The chart now has a dataset and the two drill levels.

steps.do: Choose Layout › Filter pane and add a field from the same dataset, such as channel.
steps.see: A labelled filter appears. The bound chart should respond to that field.

steps.do: Switch to Interact. Pick one filter choice, double-click a region, and use the breadcrumb and Reset to return.
steps.see: The chart first changes scope, then breaks the selected region down by state. Check that you can return to the starting view.

title: Make the layout consistent
goal: Apply a readable, repeatable design and use the right units.

steps.do: Choose Design › Region & currency. Set United States, USD and thousand/million/billion.
steps.see: The preview shows US separators and K/M/B abbreviations. Currency formatting is optional.

steps.do: Choose Design › Edit theme. Set a primary colour and a body font. Apply.
steps.see: The theme is applied. Read the smallest text and check status colours are still meaningful.

steps.do: Run the brand and accessibility checks. Fix one clear issue, such as a missing title or an unreadable colour.
steps.see: The chosen issue is gone when you run the check again.

title: Review with someone else in mind
goal: Write feedback that a teammate can act on without asking you to explain it.

steps.do: Choose Comment. Click a chart, write one specific requested change and add it.
steps.see: The note appears in Comments and clicking it takes you back to the chart.

steps.do: Add a reply with the expected result. Mark the note resolved only after checking the result.
steps.see: The note has a clear decision trail. Open and resolved filters show the right items.

steps.do: Open Prompt to preview how the comment turns into instructions. Keep the practice content local.
steps.see: The prompt names the part, describes the change and lists a check you could perform.

title: Preview a monthly refresh
goal: Replace a small practice dataset without losing a chart’s settings.

steps.do: Download the practice October CSV. Use Data › Load data to add it. Open Data › Manage and find the new dataset.
steps.see: The practice dataset has three rows and is embedded.

steps.do: Download the November CSV. In Data › Manage use Refresh from file next to the practice dataset. Pick November.
steps.see: The preview shows three → four rows, October → November, and NetSales totals of 300 → 410. No data changes yet.

steps.do: Apply the preview. Check the rows under Manage, then choose Undo.
steps.see: After applying there are four rows. Undo restores three rows. A browser recovery version is available if storage works.

title: Draft, run and read test coverage
goal: Learn what planned, ran, passed and stale mean.

steps.do: Choose Testing › Draft tests › Quick draft. Open Coverage before running anything.
steps.see: The plan has cases, while executed and passed checks are still zero on a fresh practice copy.

steps.do: Open the test plan and run it. Review one result and anything that needs a person.
steps.see: The result says what ran and what was observed. A failed or partial result is not a pass.

steps.do: Edit the heading again and reopen Coverage.
steps.see: Results for the earlier revision are stale. Run the relevant checks again when your edits are ready.

title: Verify numbers against a source
goal: Compare independent expectations and avoid certifying values you did not supply.

steps.do: Choose Testing › Numbers › Download the numbers as Excel. Inspect the columns.
steps.see: Each row identifies a chart point or KPI. The values already in the workbook are a starting template, not independent evidence.

steps.do: For practice only, change one chart value and clear the other Value cells. Import it as expected numbers.
steps.see: The import matches one value. The other values remain unverified. In real work, use the number from your independent source.

steps.do: Run the case for that chart and read the mismatch. Correct the practice workbook or remove the practice expectation.
steps.see: The result names the value it checked and the mismatch. Nothing claims that other figures matched the source.

title: Prepare a handout and a presentation
goal: Check what a reader sees and what stays in the working file.

steps.do: Add a speaker note from the tab’s menu. Rename the tab and open Presenter view.
steps.see: The note stays with the renamed tab. Use Esc to exit.

steps.do: Use Consulting › PDF or PowerPoint on the practice file. Open the output.
steps.see: Tabs become pages or slides; chart pictures are legible at normal size. Review the footer and no missing content.

title: Export and check a standalone copy
goal: Save, reopen and verify the exact file you would share.

steps.do: Choose File › Ready to publish? and read the findings. Under Offline check, download the test copy.
steps.see: The file opens without the editor. Disconnect and visit its tabs, filters and chart pop-ups before recording a pass.

steps.do: Export HTML with a new filename. Open that export in a browser and check it shows just the dashboard.
steps.see: The file opens without the editor. It can also reopen in Mothership for editing.

steps.do: Save the validation record. For a viewer release, set a version and as-of date under Publish and check that separate file.
steps.see: The record identifies a working revision and what was checked. The published copy has the intended data, comments and release details.

title: Build and apply a recipe
goal: Turn a repeatable report edit into a recipe you can use next month.

steps.do: Open Plugins › Recipe workshop and choose Executive review pack. Hover or focus the question-mark help beside Make it yours.
steps.see: The list describes the edits in plain language and the pop-up explains how to change their order.

steps.do: Edit the Executive brief step and change its Tab title to Board brief. Save the step. Choose Check targets.
steps.see: Board brief is listed as a new tab. No dashboard edits have been applied yet.

steps.do: Choose Apply recipe, close the workshop, and open Board brief.
steps.see: The brief has a decision question and a headline prompt. Applying the same recipe again keeps the matching tab.

steps.do: Open the workshop again. Use Capture dashboard setup to create a recipe from the edited dashboard. Check the steps, then use Download recipe to save it.
steps.see: The downloaded JSON can be loaded into another workshop. You can also choose Export skill ZIP or Export plugin JS.

steps.do: Optionally choose Draft with AI. Pick Terra or Sonnet, describe one repeatable edit and preview the prompt. If you use a work assistant, paste the returned recipe back for review.
steps.see: The prompt names your chosen model. Check targets lets you review an imported draft before applying it.

title: Make a consulting chart from a layout
goal: Insert a ready-made consulting chart, write its action title and know how to undo it.

steps.do: Open Insert › Chart layouts. Type ranked in the search box and choose Ranked bars, one highlight.
steps.see: The window lists Items and Value, a Data choice and a suggested action title.

steps.do: Leave Data on Sample data. Read the suggested title, then change it to a sentence of your own that says the one thing to take away. Choose Insert.
steps.see: A horizontal bar chart with one Studio green bar, the others muted, values at the end of each bar, and your title above it.

steps.do: Press Ctrl+Z once, then Ctrl+Y.
steps.see: The whole chart and its sample data disappear in one step and come back in one step.

steps.do: Open Chart layouts again and choose Bridge (waterfall). Insert it with the sample data.
steps.see: The first and last bars are totals, increases float in green, decreases in red, and a bracket shows the change from start to end.

steps.do: Press Ctrl+S, name the version After layouts, then open File › Versions.
steps.see: The version is listed as v1 (or the next number) for this practice dashboard, with Restore, Compare, Download and Delete.

title: Reshape a chart and edit its layout
goal: Change what a chart shows after it is in: other columns, fewer bars, new names, another layout.

steps.do: Open Insert › Chart layouts, type dumbbell and choose Dumbbell: before and after. Insert it with the sample data.
steps.see: Each channel has a muted dot for 2024 and a Studio green dot for 2026, joined by a line, with an action title about the biggest move.

steps.do: With the chart selected, open Charts › Reshape. Untick Social media, type Agents as the new name for Insurance agent, move Gen AI assistant to the top with the up arrow, and choose Apply.
steps.see: Social media has gone, Gen AI assistant is the first row and Insurance agent now reads Agents.

steps.do: In Reshape, add a filter: Year is 2026. Change Chart type to Bar (horizontal) and Apply.
steps.see: A plain bar chart of 2026 only. Undo (Ctrl+Z) goes back one change at a time.

steps.do: Press Ctrl+Z until the dumbbell is back. Then choose Charts › Edit layout, then ‹ Switch layout, and pick Paired bars with the gap.
steps.see: The window keeps your data and guesses the columns for the new layout.

steps.do: Choose Update.
steps.see: The dumbbell is replaced in the same place by paired bars with the gap in each label. One Ctrl+Z brings the dumbbell back.

title: Trace insurance reserves to individual claims
goal: Compare reserve concentration and verify the figure in a fictional loss run.

steps.do: Switch to Interact and select Property under Line of business.
steps.see: The Claims card shows 5 and Outstanding USD shows 44,500.

steps.do: Double-click Property in Outstanding reserves by line, then double-click Commercial property.
steps.see: The chart shows the claims behind that coverage. Use the breadcrumb to step back.

steps.do: Open Source data and match the claim IDs to their paid and outstanding amounts. Read the Methodology tab.
steps.see: Each row is one claim. Incurred is paid plus outstanding in this sample.

steps.do: Reset the filters. Switch to Edit, then use Charts › Chart layouts to insert Loss run: paid and outstanding. Choose Claims register and match Policy year, Paid USD and Outstanding USD.
steps.see: The new layout splits each policy year into paid and outstanding. The source totals are USD 43,500 and USD 52,250.
